My review isn't about the treatment or the service, which was fine. The reception staff were friendlier than the veterinarians, who were rather curt. But ultimately, their job is to heal and rehabilitate animals, not to do public relations, and they did that for my dog. They healed him. What is INTOLERABLE is what they charge. If it's not outrageous, it's bordering on it. In my case, it was a complete rip-off, and if I can avoid it, they won't see me there again. I went there on a Monday afternoon, referred by my usual veterinary clinic, because my Westie had choked on a piece of fruit and they couldn't get it out. That's why they sent me to this clinic, since the procedure had to be done endoscopically. It wasn't emergency hours, and they don't consider themselves an emergency service, as indicated at their reception desk. Nothing about it justified the extra charge they levied. They called from my clinic, they accepted the appointment, and then there was the time it took me to find the place and get there by taxi. I arrived with the animal already sedated and prepared for what they were supposed to do (an esophagoscopy, or more clearly, an endoscopy), and for that purpose, they took him into the operating room. I nervously gave them the consent form and signed it (consent that was supposed to be related to the sedation and the procedure to be performed on the animal). I signed it just like that, still nervous. He was there for about an hour and a half in total, but they soon told me the dog was fine. And I waited until they took him to the waiting room. Everything was fine. And I was very happy. Until they brought me the bill and hit me with NINE HUNDRED AND SOME EUROS for the endoscopy. Eight hundred and something for the procedure plus about a hundred extra for the time, I think in fractions of a minute, that they said they spent breaking down the piece of fruit in his stomach so he could digest it better. And nothing else. Just ventilating him and inserting the esophageal tube for the procedure—I repeat—MORE THAN NINE HUNDRED EUROS. That's an absolute rip-off. And it's not right, because it's not worth it. Especially since the animal arrived already sedated and they barely gave it anything else. Even though they put it on the consent form, which I signed thinking it was for the sedation, as is usual. But they're taking advantage of the situation, and of course, aside from starting whatever legal action I have to take, because I'm in shock at such a huge bill, if I can avoid it—I repeat—if I can avoid it, I won't go back so I don't find myself in the predicament of not being able to pay SUCH AN OUTRAGEOUS AMOUNT, which is almost a person's entire salary in such a short time. Not everyone can afford that. Not even a cosmetic surgeon earns that much. So, as far as I'm concerned, the service was very good, correct, as it should be, but it's a RIP-OFF, an OUTRAGE, and it's intolerable that they charge those amounts. 900-plus euros for an ENDOSCOPY. Then we complain that people don't do what they should for their pets. Between franchises, multinationals, and clinics like that, it's not that you don't want to... it's that THEY MAKE IT VERY DIFFICULT. At least people should know what their fees are, because they're exorbitant. That's all. My experience.
